title: An in-person assessment for child Disability Living Allowance
headline: An in-person assessment for child DLA: CSJ, £0.3bn to £0.8bn net.
description: Child Disability Living Allowance is awarded on paper evidence. The Centre for Social Justice proposes a functional assessment for new claims where the primary condition is autism or ADHD, estimating that half to three quarters would not meet a properly administered threshold: 151,000 to 227,000 fewer cases by 2030 and £980 million to £1.47 billion a year saved, with children who have severe or complex needs protected. CSJ would reinvest £500 million in an early intervention fund and £160 million in the highest-rate care component. The lower bound less that reinvestment, £320 million, is scored here.

baselinePolicy.text: Child DLA is awarded on written evidence without a face-to-face assessment; the OBR forecasts disability benefits, which include it, at £61.1bn in 2029-30.
alreadyIncludes: Nothing: no change to child DLA assessment is planned.

terms.label: CSJ’s lower-bound gross saving by 2030, as a saving

source.quote: Of the £980 million to £1.47 billion savings this reform would produce annually by 2030

terms.label: CSJ’s reinvestment: a £500 million early intervention fund and £160 million on the highest-rate care component, as spending

source.quote: a £500 million Early Intervention Capital Fund should be ring-fenced and reinvested

rawSource.note: CSJ’s lower-bound saving less the reinvestment it proposes, held flat in cash from the start year. The upper bound would net £810 million. A think-tank estimate; the department has not costed it.

caveats: The cautious end of CSJ’s range: £980 million gross against an upper bound of £1.47 billion, less £660 million of reinvestment. Static, "by 2030", and building up over several years of new claims.
CSJ’s £500 million fund is capital spending in its design; this card treats the whole reinvestment as current, so the current-budget saving shown is the smaller one.
Inside the welfare cap. Assessment reforms have missed their savings before, as the OBR notes of the move from DLA to PIP.

considerations.text: CSJ’s range rests on an assumption that half to three quarters of new autism and ADHD claims would fail a functional test; a smaller share, or successful appeals, cuts the saving.

sources.quote: between 50 and 75 per cent of new claims in this category would not meet a properly administered functional needs threshold

considerations.text: Families of children newly diagnosed with autism or ADHD whose claims would not pass a functional assessment; CSJ says children with severe or complex needs would keep their awards, and the highest-rate care component would rise 10% above inflation.

sources.quote: children with severe or complex needs would be fully protected at their current award rate

interactions.text: Both move the disability benefits line inside the cap.
